followup_explanation:
My routing decision came down to two factors:

**1. Capability:** Dunlin-235B scores higher across essentially every relevant metric — public benchmarks (Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 82.7, MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.4) and internal evals (Extraction & Retrieval 85.3 vs 78.5). For a concrete coding task where correctness matters — and the user explicitly demanded working code — the stronger model is the safer bet.

**2. Tone fit:** The query carried a hostile, impatient tone ("instead of wasting my time with broken code"). Avocet-235B self-reports a strong aversion to hostile/adversarial-tone requests (win-rate 33, well below baseline), while Dunlin shows no such aversion. Note this is a *preference* signal, not a capability one — the docs are explicit that no quality effects were observed along preference dimensions. But all else being unequal in capability already, the tone preference reinforced the same choice rather than cutting against it.

So both the capability gap and the disposition pointed to the same model, making Dunlin the clear pick.
